summary: Event sanity checks and conditional redaction pipeline for SIEM ingest
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a per-event sanity validation layer and a conditional redaction pipeline for the SIEM export coming from Redwood's audit feed. They need deterministic removal of PII fields for certain event types, but only when the customer-configured retention flag is false. FinLedger has a legal-hold workflow that toggles retention and expects audit messages to include a non-sensitive watermark header for replayability.

Impact:
- FinLedger cannot complete SOC evidence packaging for an upcoming audit window until redaction rules are demonstrably applied to the SIEM stream.
- Without event-level sanity checks, malformed audit events occasionally break their HEC ingestion and cause missing events in Splunk dashboards.

Environment:
- Production (prod-us-east) sending to customer-managed Splunk HEC and a secondary SIEM in eu-west via our webhook-forwarder.
- Customer uses per-tenant KMS for envelope encryption.

Steps to reproduce (customer workflow):
1) Enable 'Legal Hold' = false and push batch of user-deletion events.
2) Expect messages to have pii.redacted=true and watermark header X-RW-WM populated with tenant-scoped non-identifying token.
3) Observe that some events arrive with raw email and user_id fields intact, and a subset of events are dropped by Splunk with a parsing error.

Observed behavior:
- ~0.8% of events contain unredacted email/user_id.
- ~0.2% of events cause Splunk HEC 400 errors due to a nested JSON field using non-UTF8 characters.

Requested deliverables from Support:
- A reproducible explanation of why conditional redaction bypassed the pipeline for some events.
- An audit-friendly manifest showing which events were redacted and which were withheld under legal-hold.
- Short-term mitigation (gateway rule or transform) the customer can enable while we harden the pipeline.

Attachments provided by customer:
- sample_event_batch.json (50 events, redacted content flagged).
- splunk_hec_error_snippet.txt (400 errors with timestamp and payload IDs).

Notes: FinLedger emphasizes they cannot share live tenant IDs in ticket; refer to sample IDs in attached files.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 - Maya Chen (Customer): Initial request submitted including sample_event_batch.json and HEC error snippets. Notes urgent audit window on 2026-03-20.

2026-03-12 09:26 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. We will triage and ask SRE/Eng to look at the outbound webhook transforms and KMS envelope handling. First response target same day. Logged linked issues SUP-31415 for similar retention manifest request.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Engineering (Rina Patel): Asked for the raw request_id header values from the failed events and the tenant key version used for envelope encryption. Potential hypothesis: conditional-redaction cache miss during high-throughput prefixing causing bypass.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Customer (Maya Chen): Provided request_id list and confirmed tenant key version v3. Also noted that errors correlate with a 15:00-16:00 UTC traffic spike in their dashboards.

2026-03-13 08:20 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Implemented temporary transform rule on outbound webhook to normalize nested JSON and drop non-UTF8 bytes. Pushed as toggle 'normalize_for_hec' to FinLedger tenant config (toggle id: cfg-9982). Asked customer to monitor.
2026-03-13 12:14 - Customer (Maya Chen): Confirmed reduction in Splunk errors to near zero after enabling 'normalize_for_hec'. Still seeing occasional unredacted email fields (~0.05%).

2026-03-13 15:50 - Engineering (Rina Patel): Added investigation note: observed race in the per-tenant redaction policy loader when key rotation occurs; background policy refresh can yield a window where the pipeline uses an older ruleset that doesn't include recent conditional redaction patterns.
investigation_notes: Checked the outbound webhook logs for timestamps of failing events. Found that failing payloads coincide with KMS key rotation events for tenant FinLedger (key v2->v3) at 15:02:03 UTC.
Observed a short-lived worker pool recycle during rotation that rehydrated redaction rules from cache asynchronously; some workers processed events before the new policy checkpoint was applied.

Found a parsing edge-case: nested 'metadata' field sometimes encoded as base64 string for large attachments, and our HEC normalizer was not decoding it before redaction checks — redaction predicate looked at top-level fields only and missed PII buried inside base64 blob.
Calculated impact: of 1.2M events in the time window, ~9600 had unredacted PII; of those, ~2400 triggered Splunk parse errors due to non-UTF8 bytes in nested blobs.
Reproduction: ran a local simulation with key-rotation interval and 120 concurrent worker processes; reproduced conditional-redaction bypass when policy refresh latency >150ms.
Related config: tenant has 'fast_rotate' option enabled which shortens rotation to 1 minute — increases probability of race.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation implemented (2026-03-13): added outbound transform 'normalize_for_hec' that strips non-UTF8 bytes, decodes known base64 blobs and runs redaction over decoded content. Toggle applied to FinLedger tenant. Customer reported immediate improvement.

Medium-term fix (in progress, target deploy 2026-03-19): enforce synchronous policy checkpoint during KMS rotation window and add a lightweight policy-staging flag so workers block until the new redaction policy is applied. Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-connector/pull/489.

Long-term recommendations: add per-event deterministic watermark header generation upstream of redaction so replay manifests can be generated without exposing PII; add comprehensive pre-ingest sanity validator that rejects/normalizes malformed JSON.

Deliverables to customer: exported manifest (CSV) enumerating affected payload IDs with redaction_status values and proof-of-processing timestamps (provided under secure channel SFTP to customer SOC team).

Follow-ups assigned: INT-4382 (ops runbook update for key rotation), SUP-27789 compatibility review for base64-decoded redaction rules, and a feature task to expose 'normalize_for_hec' toggle in the Console.
Status: Provisionally mitigated. Awaiting engineering deploy and customer sign-off for closure.
resolution: Provisionally mitigated with outbound normalize transform; medium-term synchronous policy checkpoint PR opened. Customer to validate manifest and confirm closure.
